key_idea: Model the automorphism as a Borel map on reals that is subadditive up to Turing reducibility. Use generic continuity to freeze two local 'addition programs'. A bounded sigma-delta-style recurrence, steered by one bit of F, then shows that four F-values compute t through the frequency of its binary choices. Category cone-avoidance removes the auxiliary generic parameters.
reason: The self-correcting recurrence is a striking, reusable device. It turns an order-theoretic statement into a frequency argument that recovers a real, and the final step (π^{-1}(a) ≤ a, then symmetry) is short and clean. Against this, the argument depends heavily on the Slaman–Woodin Borel representation and on generic-continuity and category bookkeeping, and many steps (comeager pullbacks, choosing ρ, b±, δ, nested oracle indices) only verify. That keeps it from feeling inevitable.
recognized: no (claims rigidity of the Turing degrees, an open problem; uses Slaman–Woodin's Borel representation and Sacks-style category avoidance)
